storyboard.claim: The town's willful blindness hides the predator better than any supernatural power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James standing calmly among oblivious neighbors on the highway dividing the two communities — the mask icon says the apathy is a false face the town wears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from context: the wealthy white residents across the highway will not notice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask icon tells a muted viewer the town is pretending not to see.

storyboard.claim: Mrs. Green spots James Harris's suspicious van near Six Mile when a child goes missing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mrs. Green pointing at something off-screen — the car icon is the van she sees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract apathy to a specific person who actually sees the danger.
storyboard.addedInformation: The car icon literalizes the van; Mrs. Green's worried expression says this is a threat.

storyboard.claim: Mrs. Green tells Patricia about the van — a huge personal risk for her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mrs. Green leaning close to Patricia, speaking urgently — no icon needed, the two women and the callout carry it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From seeing the van to telling someone about it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two-shot shows the interpersonal stakes: an elderly Black woman risking herself to warn a white neighbor.

storyboard.claim: Grace's reaction to the warning is complete apathy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Grace sitting unmoved, arms folded, expression blank — Patricia beside her with a pleading posture. No icon: the apathy is carried by Grace's neutral idle body.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Mrs. Green risked everything to share information; now that information hits a wall of indifference.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grace's neutral idle face reads as disinterest even on mute.

storyboard.claim: Grace literally tells Patricia not to worry because crimes in Six Mile don't matter to them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Grace talking dismissively — the callout delivers her actual words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract label of apathy to Grace's specific dismissive words.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout puts Grace's own words on screen so a muted viewer reads the dismissal.

storyboard.claim: Segregation is weaponized — geography dictates who is afforded humanity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman and James standing on the highway that divides the communities — the road icon literalizes the geographic weapon: the highway itself is the dividing line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one woman's dismissal to the systemic thesis: the zip code determines who matters.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road icon says geography IS the weapon; the highway set reinforces the divide.

storyboard.claim: Counterpoint: James is an ancient drifter, an opportunist looking for a meal, not a political actor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James walking alone against an open horizon — he's a wanderer, not a strategist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The other host pushes back on the systemic reading with a simpler animal explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The horizon set and walking action say 'drifter' to a muted viewer.

storyboard.claim: Like a bear wandering into a campsite, James didn't design the segregation he exploits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James walking through a forest — the bear-in-a-campsite analogy placed in a natural setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the opportunist framing: the predator found the system, he didn't build it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The forest set echoes the national park analogy the narrator uses.

storyboard.claim: Isn't he just a monster acting like a monster, entirely separate from human politics?
storyboard.concreteVisual: James standing still in an abstract space — stripped of context, just a figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The counterpoint's final reduction: a monster is a monster, nothing more.
storyboard.addedInformation: The abstract set removes the social context the other host just built, visually matching the argument.

callout.text: HE DIDN'T HAVE TO DESIGN IT

storyboard.claim: Sharp disagreement: not designing the system doesn't excuse exploiting it — that misunderstands systemic power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James beside an everyman figure in abstract space — the system exists around them whether James built it or not.
storyboard.onScreenText: HE DIDN'T HAVE TO DESIGN IT
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Direct rebuttal of the 'just a monster' framing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the host's key counter-argument on screen.

storyboard.claim: James Harris is the ultimate perfect employee of a racist system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James standing composed in abstract space — his stillness reads as someone fulfilling a role, not raging.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rebuttal lands on its thesis: not a rogue monster but a functionary.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the key metaphor; James's neutral idle body says 'employee doing his job.'

storyboard.claim: The path of least resistance to blood is paved by systemic racism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram: Systemic racism creates blind spots which become a hunting ground — James walking through the abstract space.
storyboard.onScreenText: Flow: Systemic racism -> Blind spots -> Hunting ground
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Structures the 'perfect employee' thesis into a causal chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: The diagram makes the system's mechanics visible without sound.

storyboard.claim: James exploits blind spots white society built for its own comfort — no hypnosis needed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James standing on a manicured street beside an oblivious everyman — the blind spot is the neighbor's turned back.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the flow diagram's logic: now we see what the blind spots look like on the ground.
storyboard.addedInformation: The everyman's idle posture reads as obliviousness.

storyboard.claim: James looked at the town's map of prejudices and realized it was a menu.
storyboard.concreteVisual: James holding notes — the 'map' he is reading as a menu. No food icon: the metaphor is about selection, not dining.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From blind spots in general to James reading the town's layout as a selection guide.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes in his hand literalize the 'map' the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: Patricia finally connects the van, the missing kids, and the strange behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia holding notes in a room — the magnifier icon says investigation, close examination.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From James reading a menu to Patricia reading the evidence against him.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier literalizes the detective work; notes in hand are her evidence.

storyboard.claim: Patricia goes to her community for help — leading to the book's most devastating scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia walking forward, determined but afraid — heading toward what the narrator calls the worst moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: She has the evidence; now she goes to present it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout primes the viewer that something terrible is coming.

storyboard.claim: The safety net Patricia thought she had completely falls apart — worse than any vampire scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia slumping, defeated — her body says the support she expected is gone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The devastating moment named in the previous beat now begins to take shape.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her slumped posture tells the muted viewer she has been broken before the scene even starts.

storyboard.claim: The scene is Slick Paley's living room, staged as an intervention against Patricia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia sitting with notes in hand, Slick beside her — a living room that feels like a trap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract collapse to the specific room where it happens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout tells the muted viewer this gathering is staged against Patricia, not for her.

storyboard.claim: Patricia sits trembling, clutching handwritten notes with all the evidence — she has the receipts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close-up of Patricia holding notes tightly — her worried face and trembling body say how much rides on this.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the room's setup to Patricia's prepared evidence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The close-up and the notes make the evidence physically visible.

storyboard.claim: Instead of her friends, Patricia is surrounded by the husbands — Carter leans forward with his professional voice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Over-shoulder from Carter leaning toward Patricia — his calm neutral face against her vulnerability.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The expected support turns into an ambush.
storyboard.addedInformation: The over-shoulder shot puts the viewer behind Carter, feeling his power over Patricia.

storyboard.claim: Carter tells Patricia in front of everyone that she is suffering from group hysteria.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter pointing at Patricia — the pointing gesture says accusation, not care. His neutral face is the patronizing calm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Carter's approach revealed: he uses a diagnosis as a weapon.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing action makes the power dynamic visible: he is accusing, not examining.

storyboard.claim: Carter publicly pathologizes her legitimate fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter speaking with composed authority, Patricia beside him diminished — his calm talk reads as professional dismissal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the diagnosis label to the act of publicly turning her fear into a symptom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the tactic the muted viewer needs to understand.

storyboard.claim: It is like watching a corporate PR firm gaslight a whistleblower into thinking they are insane.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter still talking smoothly, Patricia shrinking — the dynamic of a gaslighter and his target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator names the pattern: pathologizing becomes gaslighting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout gives the muted viewer the analogy they need.

storyboard.claim: The real horror is that your own partner will sacrifice your sanity to protect himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia and Carter side by side — but she is sad and isolated while he is composed. The two-shot makes the distance between them visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the gaslighting tactic to what it means: betrayal by the closest person.
storyboard.addedInformation: Patricia is first in cast now — the beat is about her devastation, not his power.

storyboard.claim: Carter threatens to institutionalize Patricia to protect his financial investments and social capital.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter pointing at Patricia — the chains icon says imprisonment, being locked away. His neutral face is the calm of a man who holds all the power.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From emotional betrayal to an explicit threat of confinement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains reads as bound/imprisoned — the literal threat of institutionalization.

storyboard.claim: Carter uses his professional credentials as a weapon against his own wife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter pointing authoritatively — the medical icon shows his PSYCHIATRIC credentials are the weapon he wields.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the threat of institutionalization to the tool he wields: his medical authority.
storyboard.addedInformation: The medical icon reads as clinical authority; a muted viewer sees a man weaponizing his professional credentials.

storyboard.claim: Carter forces Patricia to physically stand up in the room and face James Harris.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter pointing forcefully at Patricia — the command to stand is physical control.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract weapon of credentials to a physical act of domination.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing action reads as a command on mute.

storyboard.claim: Patricia is forced to look at James — the predator she identified — and formally apologize.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia standing stiffly, sad, facing James — her body says forced compliance, his composure says he has won.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From being forced to stand to the humiliation that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Patricia's sad idle posture reads as someone doing something against her will.

storyboard.claim: Carter shakes James's hand, smiles, and invites the vampire into the book club — their only safe space.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter and James side by side — Carter's polished smile is a social performance, not genuine joy (the narration calls it 'that polished southern smile'). The door icon says: the way in has been opened.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Patricia's humiliation to Carter literally welcoming the predator.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads as a way in — Carter opens it. His happy expression is the fake Southern smile the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: Carter uses his authority as husband and doctor to crush Patricia's resistance — a masterclass in patriarchal gaslighting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter talking with authority, Patricia diminished beside him — the dynamic of domination.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator names the pattern that the last several beats demonstrated.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout gives the thesis label to the sequence the viewer just watched.

storyboard.claim: Carter neutralizes Patricia by rendering her testimony clinically insane — then the host shifts to devil's advocate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter speaking with clinical calm — his neutral expression IS the weapon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes what Carter achieved before the host pivots to consider his perspective.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout puts Carter's diagnosis on screen for the muted viewer.

storyboard.claim: Devil's advocate: Carter is a medical doctor who deals in facts and diagnosis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter in a thinking pose — the host is momentarily granting him the benefit of rational consideration.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from condemnation to the other host's attempt to steelman Carter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The think action and callout frame Carter as a reasonable professional — the steelman the narrator is about to demolish.

storyboard.claim: From Carter's perspective, Patricia is leaping to wild conclusions about a respected investor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter speaking with concern directed at Patricia — his worried expression frames her claims as alarming to him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the steelman: what Patricia's evidence looks like from the other side.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: Carter's worried expression could read as genuine concern rather than patronizing dismissal.

storyboard.claim: The host sharply rejects the steelman: Carter is absolutely not acting rationally.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter standing still in abstract space — the callout delivers the emphatic rejection of his defense.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The steelman is demolished in two words.
storyboard.addedInformation: The highlight style emphasizes the sharp rebuttal.

storyboard.claim: Carter actively refuses to look at the evidence Patricia tries to show him — he shuts her down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Patricia reaching out with evidence, Carter turned away — her reaching body and his refusal are visible without sound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The proof that Carter is not rational: he will not even examine the evidence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Patricia reaching toward someone who won't engage reads as rejection on mute.

storyboard.claim: Carter leverages medical authority to diagnose Patricia with hysteria — a sexist weapon used for centuries to silence inconvenient women.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter pointing in abstract space — the gesture reads as accusation, and the abstract set signals the historical scope of the weapon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From refusing to look at evidence to deploying a centuries-old tool of silencing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The abstract set lifts the beat from this living room to the historical pattern.

storyboard.claim: Carter does this because acknowledging Patricia would threaten the massive real estate deal he and the husbands have with James.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter and James side by side in the room — the coin icon says money, finance. Their business relationship is the real motive.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the weapon (hysteria) to the motive (money).
storyboard.addedInformation: Coin reads as money/finance — the viewer sees the financial interest binding Carter to James.

storyboard.claim: Carter's supposed rationalism is just a polite smokescreen for his greed and disregard for his wife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter standing in abstract space — the mask icon says his public rationalism is a false face hiding greed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the financial motive to the facade that covers it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mask reads as false public face, pretending — exactly what Carter's 'rationalism' is.

storyboard.claim: Carter is not under any supernatural spell — he is just acting like a patriarchal jerk protecting himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter standing alone, ordinary, unremarkable — the horror is that nothing supernatural is needed to explain his behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The final nail: no supernatural excuse exists for Carter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout makes the absence of magic the point — his cruelty is entirely human.

storyboard.claim: Carter protects his wallet and ego — the collateral damage of his denial is catastrophic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carter holding a wallet in abstract space — the object literalizes 'his wallet' and the callout names what his protection costs others.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From no supernatural excuse to the concrete thing he is protecting: money.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wallet in hand makes the greed physical; the callout names the cost.
